'''Peyton Robert Siva Jr.''' (born October 24, 1990)<ref name=UofLSportsProfile>{{cite web |url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/siva_peyton00.html |title=Peyton Siva Bio |work=gocards.com |access-date=May 17, 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130205131748/http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/siva_peyton00.html |archive-date=February 5, 2013 }}</ref> is an American [[college basketball]] coach and former professional player. He is currently an assistant coach for the [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville Cardinals]] of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]] (ACC). He played college basketball for [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]], leading the school to two [[Final Four (college basketball)|Final Fours]], including a [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|national championship]] his [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|senior season]]. He was drafted by the [[Detroit Pistons]], who selected him with the 56th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]].

==Early life and education==
Siva is of [[Samoan American|Samoan]] descent and grew up in a troubled Seattle neighborhood. His mother worked three jobs to try to support the family. His father was mostly absent, struggling with drug and alcohol addiction throughout Siva's childhood. The younger Siva successfully talked his father out of killing himself.<ref name=Saslow>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8576564/louisville-pg-peyton-siva-returns-senior-season-lead-cardinals-espn-magazine |title=The ascent from deuce-8 |first=Eli |last=Saslow |magazine=[[ESPN The Magazine]] |date=November 12, 2012 |access-date=November 1, 2012}}</ref><!--ESPN routinely posts magazine stories online several days before the magazine print date.-->

Siva, determined to escape the fate of other family members, plunged himself into sports. When he first tried out for youth football, he was too light to play, but managed to make weight. He soon developed a reputation as a relentlessly aggressive athlete in both football and basketball, and as a promising young prospect. Siva also made it a point to avoid alcohol and drugs, and helped many other boys in his neighborhood avoid gang involvement, partially by persuading his mother to let them stay at her house on weekends.

==High school career==
Siva attended [[Franklin High School (Seattle)|Franklin High School]] in Seattle. His freshman year he averaged 13.5 points helping Franklin win the 4A championship. As a senior he averaged 18.1 points, 5.3 assists, 3.4 rebounds, and 2.3 steals,<ref name="UofLSportsProfile" /> leading Franklin to the Class 3A state championship.<ref name="HS-POY">{{cite news |url=http://seattletimes.nwsource.com/html/localnews/2009063706_apbkhwashallstateteam1stldwritethru.html |title=Siva and Moore unanimous AP players of the year  |access-date=February 2, 2011 |date= April 15, 2009|newspaper=Seattle Times}}</ref>  He was a unanimous selection for AP Washington Player of the Year,<ref name="HS-POY"/> was named a [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]],<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.seattlepi.com/preps/400795_prepbok20.html |title=Siva headlines state contingent for McDonald's All-American Game
 |access-date=February 2, 2011 |last= Fessenden|first= Darren|date= February 19, 2009|publisher=[[Seattle P-I]]}}</ref> and was named [[Washington Mr. Basketball|Mr. Basketball]] in the state of Washington.<ref name="UofLSportsProfile"/>

==College career==

===Freshman year===
During his [[2009-10 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|freshman season]] Siva averaged 11.3 minutes in 31 games backing up senior starter [[Edgar Sosa (basketball)|Edgar Sosa]].<ref name="Espn.go.com">{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/gamelog/_/id/2488706/peyton-siva |title=Peyton Siva Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=October 24, 1990 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref>  Hampered by a wrist injury throughout the year he managed to dish out at least 3 assists in 11 games and he scored a career high 14 at West Virginia. Louisville beat #1 [[2009–10 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] 78–68 in their final game of the final season at [[Freedom Hall]], before moving to the [[KFC Yum! Center]].<ref>{{cite web|author=Freedom Hall, Louisville, KY |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300650097 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411005643/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=300650097 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2013 |title=Syracuse Orange vs. Louisville Cardinals – Recap – March 06, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 6, 2010 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref> The Cardinals finished the season 20–13, and tied for 5th in the [[Big East Conference|Big East]] with an 11–7 conference record. They lost in the second round of the [[2010 Big East men's basketball tournament|Big East tournament]] to [[2009–10 Cincinnati Bearcats men's basketball team|Cincinnati]] 66–69.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=300690097 |title=Cincinnati Bearcats vs. Louisville Cardinals – Box Score – March 10, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 10, 2010 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref> Louisville received an at-large bid to the [[2010 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2010 NCAA tournament]], earning a 9 seed in the South Region where they lost to 8 seed [[2009–10 California Golden Bears men's basketball team|California]] 62–77 in the first round.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/boxscore?gameId=300780025 |title=Louisville Cardinals vs. California Golden Bears – NCAA Tournament Game – Box Score – March 19, 2010 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 19, 2010 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref>

===Sophomore year===
[[File:Peyton Siva (cropped).jpg|250px|thumb|right|Siva playing with Louisville]]
In his [[2010-11 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|sophomore season]] he started 35 games for the Cardinals, averaging 28 minutes a game.<ref name="Espn.go.com"/> He averaged 9.9 points per game and his 5.2 assists per game ranked second best in the Big East.<ref name="University of Louisville">{{cite web|title=2011–12 Louisville Basketball Media Guide|url=http://www.guide.provations.com/louisville/2011mensbasketball#pg64|work=Player Bio: Peyton Siva|publisher=University of Louisville|access-date=January 29, 2012|archive-date=June 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120613210253/http://www.guide.provations.com/louisville/2011mensbasketball#pg64|url-status=dead}}</ref> In consecutive games against [[West Virginia Mountaineers men's basketball|West Virginia]] and [[2010-11 Connecticut Huskies men's basketball team|Connecticut]], Siva hit game-winning layups in the final seconds to give Louisville one-point victories.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310260097 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110129005612/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310260097 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 29, 2011 |title=Peyton Siva's layup helps Louisville tip West Virginia |access-date=February 2, 2011 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310290041 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120709194052/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310290041 |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 9, 2012 |title=Peyton Siva outshines Kemba Walker as Louisville edges Connecticut |access-date=February 2, 2011 |publisher=[[ESPN]]}}</ref> He was an honorable mention selection for the 2011 All-Big East Men's Basketball Team<ref>{{cite web|title=All-BIG EAST Men's Basketball Teams Announced|url=http://www.bigeast.org/News/tabid/435/Article/221858/all-big-east-mens-basketball-teams-announced.aspx|publisher=Big East Conference|access-date=January 28, 2012}}</ref> and was named to the [[2011 Big East men's basketball tournament]] All-Tournament Team after averaging 12 points, 7.7 assists, and 5.3 rebounds as the Cardinals reached the championship game.<ref name="University of Louisville"/> The Cardinals finished the season 25–10, 12–6 in the [[2010–11 Big East Conference men's basketball season|2010–11 Big East season]] tied for 3rd in the conference. They received an at-large bid and a #4 seed in the [[2011 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2011 NCAA tournament]] where they were upset in the first round by #13 seeded [[2010–11 Morehead State Eagles men's basketball team|Morehead State]] 61–62.<ref>{{cite web|author=Pepsi Center, Denver, CO |url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310760097 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130411013359/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=310760097 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 11, 2013 |title=Morehead State Eagles vs. Louisville Cardinals – NCAA Tournament Game – Recap – March 17, 2011 – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=March 17, 2011 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref>

===Junior year===
During his junior year in [[2011-12 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|2011–12]], Siva had difficulties on the court early in the season; midway through the season, he had made less than 25% of his three-point attempts, and turned the ball over as much as four times in one half.<ref name=Saslow/> Cardinals coach [[Rick Pitino]] sensed that Siva was getting involved in too many things, and pulled him aside for a talk. Pitino later recalled, "I told him, 'Take a relationship sabbatical — I'll even call your girlfriend for you.' He should only be making time for two things: school and basketball. I told him that we need 100 percent of his focus on the court."<ref name=Saslow/> From that point, Siva rediscovered his game, and became the Most Outstanding Player of the [[2012 Big East men's basketball tournament|2012 Big East tournament]]. In the tournament he averaged 13.8 points and 5.8 assists per game. Louisville advanced to the Final Four of the [[2012 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2012 NCAA tournament]], upsetting #1 seed [[2011–12 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] 57–44 in the sweet sixteen and defeating #7 seed [[2011–12 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the regional final. Before losing in the national semifinals to [[Kentucky–Louisville rivalry|arch-rival]] and eventual national champion [[2011–12 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Kentucky]].<ref name="Espn.go.com"/> Siva averaged 9.1 points, 3.2 rebounds, 5.6 assists, and 1.7	steals a game for the Cardinals, who finished the season with a 30–10 record.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/2488706/peyton-siva |title=Peyton Siva Stats, News, Videos, Highlights, Pictures, Bio – Louisville Cardinals – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=October 24, 1990 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref>

===Senior year===
[[Image:Russ Smith Peyton Siva championship trophy.jpg|thumb|right|200px|[[Russ Smith (basketball)|Russ Smith]] (left) and Siva (right) with the [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] trophy.]]
Before the start of the [[2012–13 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2012–13 basketball season]] the [[2012–13 Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team|Louisville Cardinals men's basketball team]] was picked to finish 1st in the [[2012–13 Big East Conference men's basketball season|Big East Conference]] in polls done by Big East writers<ref>{{cite web|author=Central New York |url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2012/10/louisville_tops_big_east_write.html |title=Louisville tops Big East writers' poll; Cardinals dominate all-league teams |date=October 17, 2012 |publisher=syracuse.com |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref> and coaches.<ref>{{cite web|last=Smith |first=Jared |url=http://newyork.sbnation.com/2012/10/17/3517762/big-east-basketball-media-day-2012-coaches-poll-all-big-east-preseason |title=Big East basketball media day: Coaches' poll, All-Big East preseason teams and news – SB Nation New York |publisher=Newyork.sbnation.com |date=October 17, 2012 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref> Siva was selected as the Big East Preseason Player of the Year and to the Big East Preseason first team by both the writers and coaches also. Louisville finished the regular season with a 26–5 record and 14–4 in the Big East to tie for a share of the Big East regular season championship with [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] and [[2012–13 Marquette Golden Eagles men's basketball team|Marquette]], who also finished with a 14–4 conference record.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ennis |first=Mark |url=https://www.sbnation.com/college-basketball/2013/3/12/4091940/2013-big-east-tournament-preview-louisville-georgetown-syracuse-otto-porter |title=2013 Big East tournament preview: Louisville and Georgetown favorites in league's swan song |publisher=SBNation.com |date=March 12, 2013 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref>  Siva led Louisville to the [[2013 Big East men's basketball tournament|2013 Big East tournament]] championship and was named the tournament's most outstanding player for the second consecutive year. Siva became the second player ever to win this award multiple times; [[Patrick Ewing]] accomplished the same feat in 1984 and 1985<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.syracuse.com/orangebasketball/index.ssf/2013/03/louisvilles_peyton_siva_joins.html|title=Louisville's Peyton Siva joins Georgetown's Patrick Ewing as the only two-time winners of the Big East Most Outstanding Player award|date=March 17, 2013 |publisher=Syracuse Post-Standard}}</ref> Siva had a Big East tournament and school record for steals in a Big East tournament game with seven vs [[2012–13 Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball team|Notre Dame]] in the semi-finals, it tied [[Terrence Williams]] (also from Seattle, WA) the only other Louisville player and 10 others.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031613aaf.html |title=Louisville-Notre Dame Postgame Notes – Louisville Cardinals Official Athletic Site |publisher=Gocards.com |access-date=April 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141020163336/http://www.gocards.com/sports/m-baskbl/recaps/031613aaf.html |archive-date=October 20, 2014 |url-status=dead }}</ref> The seven steals made him Louisville's all-time career leader with 236 steals, at that time, he passed [[Darrell Griffith]]'s record of 230 he had from 1976 to ==Professional career==

===Detroit Pistons (2013–2014)===
Siva was drafted 56th overall in the [[2013 NBA draft]] by the [[Detroit Pistons]]. In July 2013, he joined the Pistons for the [[2013 NBA Summer League]]. On August 5, 2013, he signed with the Pistons.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/08/05/pistons-sign-siva.ap/|title=Pistons sign Siva|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 5, 2013|access-date=August 5, 2013}}</ref> On December 26, 2013, he was assigned to the Fort Wayne Mad Ants.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14979 |title=Detroit Pistons assign Tony Mitchell and Peyton Siva to D-League |access-date=December 27, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924044545/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=14979 |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 13, 2014, he was recalled by the Pistons.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15069 |title=Detroit Pistons recall Peyton Siva and Tony Mitchell from D-League |access-date=January 13, 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924044613/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=15069 |archive-date=September 24, 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 31, 2014, he was reassigned to the Mad Ants.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/pistons-re-assign-peyton-siva-and-tony-mitchell-ft-wayne-mad-ants Pistons Re-Assign Peyton Siva and Tony Mitchell to Ft. Wayne Mad Ants]</ref> He was recalled in mid-February 2014.

On July 15, 2014, he was waived by the Pistons following the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/127386/pistons-waive-peyton-siva-and-josh-harrellson.html Pistons waive Peyton Siva and Josh Harrellson]</ref><ref>[http://www.mlive.com/pistons/index.ssf/2014/07/detroit_pistons_release_peyton.html Detroit Pistons release Peyton Siva, Josh Harrellson from their non-guaranteed contracts]</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2014)===
On September 29, 2014, Siva signed with the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=16633 Orlando Magic add Kadeem Batts, Drew Crawford, Seth Curry, Peyton Siva to training camp]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Magic on October 25, 2014.<ref>[http://www.orlandopinstripedpost.com/2014/10/25/7070417/orlando-magic-training-camp-2014-roster-cuts-peyton-siva-seth-curry Orlando Magic training camp: Team waives Seth Curry, Peyton Siva, and two others]</ref> On October 30, 2014, Siva was acquired by the [[Erie BayHawks (2008–2017)|Erie BayHawks]] as an affiliate player.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_acquire_four_players_2014_10_30.html BayHawks Acquire Four Players, Complete Coaching Staff] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160610055533/http://www.nba.com/dleague/erie/bayhawks_acquire_four_players_2014_10_30.html |date=June 10, 2016 }}</ref>

===Juvecaserta Basket (2015–2016)===
On August 12, 2015, Siva signed with [[Juvecaserta Basket]] of the Italian [[Lega Basket Serie A|Serie A]] for the 2015–16 season.<ref>{{cite news|title=Caserta announces Peyton Siva|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/172472/caserta-announces-peyton-siva.html|access-date=August 12, 2015|work=Sportando.com|date=August 12, 2015}}</ref> Siva led the Serie A in assists, as he had 6.5 per game.

===Alba Berlin (2016–2021)===
On June 22, 2016, Siva signed a two-year deal with [[Alba Berlin]].<ref>{{cite news|title=NCAA-Champ Peyton Siva unterschreibt für zwei Jahre|url=https://www.albaberlin.de/news/ncaa-champ-peyton-siva-unterschreibt-fuer-zwei-jahre-7021.html|access-date=June 26, 2016|work=Albaberlin.de|date=June 22, 2016|language=de|archive-date=August 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160812204753/https://www.albaberlin.de/news/ncaa-champ-peyton-siva-unterschreibt-fuer-zwei-jahre-7021.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> For Berlin, Siva has been the starting point guard and has guided the team to two [[Basketball Bundesliga|BBL championships]], in 2020 and 2021. In 2018, he was named to the [[All-Basketball Bundesliga Team]].

===New Zealand Breakers (2021–2022)===
On August 22, 2021, Siva signed with the [[New Zealand Breakers]] for the [[2021–22 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Breakers Confirm Peyton Siva Signing|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-confirm-peyton-siva-signing|access-date=August 22, 2021|website=NBL.com.au|date=August 22, 2021|language=en}}</ref> He suffered a grade 2 hamstring tear in the second game of the season was ruled out for up to eight weeks.<ref>{{cite news|last=Hinton|first=Marc|title=NZ Breakers 'evaluating' Peyton Siva situation as they search for NBL turnaround|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/300477001/nz-breakers-evaluating-peyton-siva-situation-as-they-search-for-nbl-turnaround|access-date=December 13, 2021|website=stuff.co.nz|date=December 13, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Breakers Add Experienced NBA Guard as Injury Replacement|url=https://nbl.com.au/news/breakers-add-experienced-nba-guard-as-injury-replacement|website=NBL.com.au|date=December 15, 2021|access-date=December 15, 2021|quote=Walsh says Siva's hamstring tear could keep him out of action for up to eight weeks.}}</ref> He returned to action on January 9, 2022.<ref>{{cite news|title=Yanni Wetzell leads the way as NZ Breakers break season duck against Brisbane Bullets|url=https://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/basketball/127459772/yanni-wetzell-leads-the-way-as-nz-breakers-break-season-duck-against-brisbane-bullets|access-date=January 9, 2022|website=stuff.co.nz|date=January 9, 2022}}</ref>

===Panathinaikos (2022)===
On April 28, 2022, Siva signed with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] for the rest of the 2021–22 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.paobc.gr/deltia-typoy/103073_ston-panathinaiko-opap-o-siba|title=Στον Παναθηναϊκό ΟΠΑΠ ο Σίβα|work=paobc.gr|date=April 28, 2022|access-date=April 29, 2022}}</ref> In 12 league games, he averaged 2.9 points, 2.4 rebounds and 3.2 assists, playing around 17 minutes per contest.

===Illawarra Hawks (2022–2023)===
On October 19, 2022, Siva signed with the [[Illawarra Hawks]] for the rest of the [[2022–23 NBL season]].<ref>{{cite news|title=The Hawks Swoop on Siva|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/the-hawks-swoop-on-siva|access-date=October 19, 2022|website=hawks.com.au|date=October 19, 2022}}</ref> On January 5, 2023, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after suffering a right shoulder injury. He sustained a high-grade [[Acromioclavicular joint|AC joint]] injury in the Hawks' New Year's Eve game against the [[Perth Wildcats]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Illawarra Hawks Roster Update - Peyton Siva|url=https://www.hawks.com.au/news/illawarra-hawks-roster-update-peyton-siva|access-date=January 6, 2023|website=hawks.com.au|date=January 5, 2023}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Siva is a devout [[Christianity|Christian]] and is involved with Louisville's Fellowship of Christian Athletes. After Siva successfully talked his father out of suicide, the two have become close, according to the younger Siva. His father gave up other drugs shortly after the suicide attempt; while he has continued to struggle with alcohol, family members say his condition has steadily improved.<ref name=Saslow/> Every year during his son's college career, his father came to Louisville to spend the season with his son, and was a fixture at Cardinals home games.<ref name=Saslow/> His siblings have also abandoned their previous criminal activity, and his mother, who had worked three jobs while he was growing up, is now a drug counselor.<ref name=Saslow/> Siva was one of the top searched college basketball players in his final season at Louisville.<ref>{{cite web|author=Lisa Olson |url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-03-14/ncaa-tournament-2012-louisville-guard-peyton-sivas-most-important-drive-came-off |title=Louisville guard Peyton Siva Jr.'s most important drive came off the court – NCAA Basketball – Sporting News |publisher=Aol.sportingnews.com |date=March 14, 2012 |access-date=April 9, 2013}}</ref>

Shortly after his graduation, he married his longtime girlfriend, Patience McCroskey, on July 27, 2013, at Louisville's home arena, the [[KFC Yum! Center]], in a large reception room that overlooks the [[Ohio River]]. The wedding was the first to be held at the arena.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.courier-journal.com/article/20130719/SPORTS02/307190089/Former-Louisville-basketball-player-Peyton-Siva-s-Yum-Center-wedding-arena-s-first |title=Former Louisville basketball player Peyton Siva's Yum! Center wedding the arena's first |first=Jonathan |last=Lintner |newspaper=[[The Courier-Journal]] |date=July 19, 2013 |access-date=August 2, 2013}} (soft paywall)</ref>
